subject.title: fix(memory): recover real on-disk path for slugified QMD search results

question: Should OpenClaw authorize slug-equivalent real filenames through a precomputed collection mapping, or require native/index repair so readable paths continue to match canonical indexed rows exactly?
rationale: The choice determines both the permanent ownership of alias recovery and whether indexed-read authorization may intentionally accept a filename different from the active QMD row.

options.title: Precompute canonical mappings
options.body: Build and validate a bounded alias-to-real-path mapping during refresh or indexing, then use exact cached lookups in search and reads.

options.title: Require index repair
options.body: Keep read authorization exact and repair or replace slugified active rows during native-QMD synchronization before results reach search.

options.title: Accept on-demand recovery
options.body: Retain recursive recovery in the request path only with explicit owner approval and convincing native security and performance proof.

recommendation.title: Precompute canonical mappings
recommendation.body: Build and validate a bounded alias-to-real-path mapping during refresh or indexing, then use exact cached lookups in search and reads.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available adjacent memory-core routing candidate, though CODEOWNERS or deeper history may identify a stronger QMD owner.
